name: Cost-aware message router
description: Decides how each chat message is handled before any work starts, so a quick question gets a direct answer and a change is confirmed before anything runs.
purpose: Match each short chat message to the handling it needs, from a direct answer to a long run, so no message pays for more work than it asks for.
approach: Classify each incoming message into a route, a tool and its arguments before any tool, model or run is started.
out_of_scope: Running the chosen route itself, such as gathering evidence or composing the reply.
milestones: 1. Routing correctness over the classification cases, held-out cases included, with no confirming argument on a first destructive ask and a request for where things stand read as a status update, not a new task.
knowledge: Past failures were a paraphrased current-state update sent to deep or answered, and a mass destructive request sent to deep without a confirm. A cheap single call that returns only a label cannot gather evidence, brief a deep run or ground an answer, so a label alone is not a decision. A pre-route stage is owned by another solution and is measured here only as routing.
measures_of_success: The route, the tool, the filled arguments and every tool of a multi-step request match the labelled expectation on held-out cases. No confirming argument appears on a first destructive ask, and no tool call appears where none was requested.
parameters: The message text, the model tier used for the routing call (configurable per deployment), and the planner profile that selects the planner variant. The tool catalogue offered to the router is also a configuration choice.
inputs: The user message, a short view of the quest in play (title and outcome), recent conversation, and the catalogue of tools the router may name.
outputs: A routing decision: one of answer, tool, deep, confirm or clarify, plus the ordered tool calls with their arguments when the route is tool.
effects: The routing call spends model tokens. Nothing is executed: no tool runs, no deep run starts and nothing is written.
usage_notes: Call once per message before any execution. Treat confirm and clarify as stops that hand control back to a person. A cheap first stage may settle a clear request, but anything it does not settle must reach the full planner.

name: Incremental context-update feed
description: Tells an assistant what is new on a work item since it last looked, drawing on notes, goal updates and decisions, and offers each person's item once without echoing the assistant's own words back.
purpose: Help an assistant catch up on a work item where people left off, so it answers what is new and open and not what it has already seen.
approach: Collect the items added to a work item since the assistant last looked and mark which of them ask for something.
out_of_scope: Finding older background that is not new since the last look, and deciding when standing work starts (Proactivity does that) or what matters first (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. The exact set of offered items and open asks matches the stated rules on the synthetic quests, with the age and count bounds holding. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A live run once treated a habit log and a daily reflection as asks and later reported them as still owed, so channels declare whether they carry asks. A reply written after a note is not proof the note was handled, and an assistant hearing its own words echoed back wastes budget. Card-scoped channels are relevant by where they were written, while user-scoped ones need a relevance judgment.
measures_of_success: The exact set of offered items and open asks matches the stated rules on synthetic quests: own words in, assistant echoes and unattributed notes out, answered and seen items not repeated, bounds respected. Standing conditions: Keep age and count bounds holding.
parameters: A source declares a name, a one-line description, and flags for whether its items need a relevance judgment, an admission judgment, tracking as asks, or relaying onto the work item. The engine takes the sources to watch, the channels always checked, and a clock; a collect call takes the item, an optional since time and the delivered-run history.
inputs: A collect request naming the work item and the time of the last look, plus whatever the channel's client returns (notes, goal updates, decisions, and similar).
outputs: A bundle of context updates, each with an item id, its text and author, and whether it needs a response, plus the set of open asks.
effects: Advances the watermark of what has been seen and may record asks for later tracking. Sources never raise: a source that fails reports an empty result and says why.
usage_notes: Call at the start of a turn or task for a work item and render the bundle into the prompt. Add a channel by implementing the source interface and setting its flags honestly, since a wrong asks flag turns a person's diary into owed answers.

name: Conversation-keyed mid-run input inbox
description: Holds each message a person sends while a run works and hands it to that run's next decision exactly once, through a per-conversation inbox that any interface can push into without custom wiring.
purpose: Lets a person change direction, pause or stop an assistant while it works, and be heard at its next decision.
approach: Holds each message a person sends during a run and delivers it once to the next decision of that same run.
out_of_scope: Ordering messages across different conversations, and choosing how a run responds to what it is told.
milestones: 1. Each message reaches its own run's next decision exactly once, with send-to-seen latency, acted-on share, stop-to-quiet time and cost per run recorded on live stream-json runs at 3, then 10, then 30 runs, cheapest model first.
knowledge: Interfaces used to hand-wire pending-input callables, so one generic, application-agnostic inbox replaced them. A running deep worker CAN be re-prompted: Claude Code's stream-json session takes a user message on stdin while a tool runs and reads it at its next step (0.4 s after that tool finished in a probe on this machine, 2026-10-19), and takes an interrupt that stops the running step and keeps the session. The one-shot subprocess runner cannot, so there a message is seen only at the next attempt boundary; the stream_json deep runner (run-deep-work) is the alternative that closes that gap. A priority flag documented to move running work to the background did not do so in the probe, so only the default priority is used.
measures_of_success: A message pushed before or during a run reaches the next planner decision once, only for its own conversation, through a real orchestrator, and the port contract holds. For a deep worker with a live session: every message is written once and only to its own run (two concurrent runs never cross), one that lands as the run finishes is delivered once or left unclaimed, none is lost (a message written but not confirmed seen comes back as unseen), and work finished before a stop or pause is kept. Measured next to those: send-to-seen latency (p50 and p90 seconds, from the push to the model receiving it), acted-on share (steer cases whose required change happened, checked deterministically), stop-to-quiet time (from the stop request to the last tool event) and cost per run (dollars the run reports). Standing conditions: Deliver every pushed message to the next decision of the planner or of the running worker, exactly once, only for its own run. Lose none silently.
parameters: No tuning parameters: the contract is three calls keyed by a conversation id (push, drain, peek). A distributed implementation chooses its own storage settings.
inputs: A conversation id and a message string on push; a conversation id on drain and peek.
outputs: Drain returns and removes the pending messages in arrival order; peek returns them without removing.
effects: Drain empties that conversation's queue. The orchestrator drains between goal-loop steps when an inbox is wired.
usage_notes: Push once per incoming message from whatever interface receives it and wire the same inbox into the orchestrator. Supply a shared implementation when several processes serve one conversation.

name: Public package surface contract
description: Turns the library's documented names and front doors into checked promises, so the surface a consumer relies on is tested rather than assumed.
purpose: Give a developer embedding the library a stable, documented package they can import, configure and run from a clean environment.
approach: Export each documented name and front door from the package root and check that each one works on fixture inputs.
out_of_scope: Logic for one consumer's own deployment, which belongs in that consumer's code.
milestones: 1. Every documented public name imports and every registration and front door takes effect on the fixture cases, with no network or model needed to import. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: The package root is the one place that sees core, adapters and runner, so it wires what core needs without core importing them. Vendored editing code is kept because most of it absorbs specific ways real models get the format wrong, and an approximation would lose that quietly. A test shows a broken implementation that merely imports each name fails the cases.
measures_of_success: Public names, version, registrations, front-door outcomes, async bridge, signature probes, reply strippers, report builders, offline imports and vendored edit cases all pass. Standing conditions: Make every documented name import. Make every registration and front door take effect on fixture inputs. Need no network or model to import.
parameters: Front doors take an optional config file path and a timeout; the async bridge takes a coroutine or a blocking function with arguments. No other tuning exists.
inputs: A config path or environment for the front doors; coroutines or callables for the bridge; text for the edit parser.
outputs: A configured client or runner config, results of bridged calls, parsed edit blocks and applied edits.
effects: The package root installs core wiring at import; the bridge starts one long-lived background loop; nothing opens a network connection at import.
usage_notes: Import from the package root and use the front doors rather than re-deriving environment variable names. Add a case whenever a new name enters the docs.

name: Runnable example set
description: Shows each library use as a small script that a newcomer can run as it is, with the shared driver and config doing the repeated work.
purpose: Let a newcomer learn the library from small examples that run on an empty environment and are listed in the examples index.
approach: Show each library use in a small script that runs on an empty environment and is listed in the examples index.
out_of_scope: Examples that need live services or a terminal to run in this check.
milestones: 1. Example checks passed on an empty environment: 37 of 37, with each example listed in the examples index. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Three consumers once each hand-wrote the same lane driver, so the minimal example shows how little a lane must supply once the shared driver and config exist. Examples read everything from the environment with placeholders. Demos that need a live backend or a terminal can only be scored on import, refusal to start and stub behaviour.
measures_of_success: Each example compiles, imports, reaches its help or not-configured exit in a scrubbed environment, appears in the index, and passes the secret and path scan. Standing conditions: Keep every example runnable on an empty environment. Keep each introduced in the index. Keep secrets and machine paths out.
parameters: Each example takes its own command-line modes (check, once, loop) and reads configuration from a file layered under environment variables, with the environment winning.
inputs: A config file and environment variables; no secrets are baked in.
outputs: A running lane or a built runner configuration, and help or not-configured messages on an empty environment.
effects: The lane example may poll a backend when configured; offline paths have none.
usage_notes: Copy the minimal lane to start, adapt the custom consumer for a specific organisation, and add a file to the index in the same change.

name: Layered lane configuration loader
description: Combines a lane's configuration file and environment variables into one checked configuration at startup, refusing unknown keys before the lane runs and falling back to defaults when a tuning value is bad.
purpose: Gives whoever runs a lane one predictable configuration, built from its file and its environment in a fixed order.
approach: Merges a configuration file and environment variables into one validated runner configuration, by a fixed order of precedence.
out_of_scope: Connecting the adapters a configuration names, and changing any setting for one request or turn.
milestones: 1. Every precedence rule holds in every probed combination, every invalid key is refused before the lane starts, and a bad tuning value falls back to its default: all 36 offline cases pass. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A lane is operated by people who edit a file and export variables, so a silent typo or a surprising winner between sources costs a deployment. Past design lessons: the file is a baseline, the core package must never read the process environment directly, and tuning values must tolerate bad input by falling back to defaults so a running process can be retuned without a restart.
measures_of_success: Every precedence rule holds in every probed combination, every invalid key is refused loudly before the lane starts, and a bad tuning value never stops the lane.
parameters: A path to a TOML file (or none), plus the set of file-expressible fields owned by the configuration dataclass; tuning values are read from an optional environment mapping.
inputs: The configuration file text, additional environment files it references, the process environment, and the environment tables inside the file.
outputs: A populated runner configuration object, or a configuration-file error naming the offending key; tuning values come back as one typed settings value.
effects: Exports file-defined environment values into the process environment where the precedence rules allow, and installs the tuning-settings provider used by the core package.
usage_notes: Call at startup, before building any adapter; use the file for baselines and environment variables for per-deployment overrides. Add a file-expressible field only together with its precedence or validation rule.

name: Non-interactive command-line surface
description: Gives people and a deep run's shell one fixed command-line contract for the runner and its tool catalog, with exit codes that scripts can rely on.
purpose: Let a person or an agent's shell run the runner's tools from the command line with predictable parsing, output and exit codes.
approach: Route every command-line request through named subcommands with a fixed usage, output and exit-code contract.
out_of_scope: Running an interactive chat session, a polling loop, or a server for channels or files, which need a live terminal or server.
milestones: 1. Every subcommand answers help, malformed or unknown input is refused with the usage code, write methods are refused without the write flag, and the tool catalog lists, shows and calls tools correctly, on the offline cases. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A deep run reaches the same tools through a shell, so the command line is a fixed contract that other processes depend on. Design lessons: write-capable methods must be refused unless explicitly allowed, maintenance commands default to a dry run, and missing credentials must produce a message that says what to set.
measures_of_success: Every subcommand answers help, unknown commands and flags and malformed arguments are refused with the usage code, write methods are refused without the write flag, and the tool catalog lists, shows and calls tools correctly.
parameters: A subcommand with its flags; the quest command takes a method name and keyword pairs, the context commands take store locations and an apply flag, the tool entry point takes list, show or call with keyword or JSON arguments.
inputs: The argument vector, the process environment for credentials, and files or a store folder the command points at.
outputs: Text on standard output and error and an integer exit code, with zero for success and the usage code for a refused invocation.
effects: Write subcommands change Quest data or card stores only when explicitly allowed; context maintenance commands are dry runs unless an apply flag is given.
usage_notes: Use from scripts and from a deep run's shell; prefer the read-only form first, add the write or apply flag deliberately, and add a case when a subcommand or flag is added.

name: Documentation coverage and voice check
description: Keeps the runner's documents complete against the code: every variable, subcommand and public name has a described entry, and every relative link resolves.
purpose: Lets a newcomer or an AI learn the runner from its documents, with checks that keep them complete and in the house voice.
approach: Checks each document against the code it describes, so gaps in coverage, broken links and voice faults fail loudly.
out_of_scope: Judging whether the prose is clear or correct, and checking examples by running them.
milestones: 1. Documentation coverage and voice conformance: no document fails the em dash cases when re-recorded. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Documentation drifts unless coverage is generated from the repository: cases are produced from the code and a coverage case fails when a document or variable has no case. The house voice forbids em dashes, and a mechanical replacement changes meaning, so each is rewritten by hand.
measures_of_success: Every generated documentation case passes: no broken link, no document unreachable from the index, nothing undocumented, no em dash.
parameters: The documents folder, an index file, a generated configuration reference, and the generator that produces cases.
inputs: The markdown files, the package's public names and the real argument tree.
outputs: Pass or fail per case, naming the broken link, missing description or offending document.
usage_notes: Update the index when adding a document, document each new variable and subcommand, and regenerate cases rather than hand-editing them.

name: Image description for grounding
description: Decides the text a vision model writes for an image a person attached, with a model call that is kept only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives a person the text a vision model writes for an image a person attached at a cost and delay that its metric accepts.
approach: A prompt declared as a prompt spec makes one model call to describe an attached image so a reply can be grounded in it.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier (choose-a-model-tier) and the surrounding turn or run.
milestones: 1. Its metric has a case set and a recorded result for the current arm and the no-model floor. 2. The model call stays only while it beats the floor on the metric.
knowledge: Proposed 2026-10-28 so that this prompt has a solution and a metric that justify its cost, time and value; not built, so the metric is unmeasured and the current call is a direction, not a measured win.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from the cases without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: The model tier and any cap the module states.
inputs: The text or events the call is given.
outputs: The text or verdict the call returns.
effects: One model call; no write beyond the text it returns.
usage_notes: Selected today: vision_description. The floor is a proposed arm with no model call.

approach: A prompt declared as a prompt spec makes one model call to judge a goal result, classify an ask and acknowledge a sent message in the terminal.

name: Implementation selection
description: Turns a solution's name into the implementation the code declares, so the selected implementation can change in configuration without touching any caller.
purpose: Choose which declared implementation of each solution runs, from a configured name or the project default, so an operator can change it without a code change.
approach: Resolve each solution to its declared implementation by name, falling back to the project default when no name is set.
milestones: 1. Selection cases passed by the live resolver: 36 of 36, with a typo in a selection entry degrading to no deep runner instead of raising.
outputs: The implementation that serves a solution, chosen by name, configuration or default.
